Rashi on Menachot 9b:10:1.hebrew: סלת עשרון - בעי לוג שמן, דאמר בפ' שתי מדות (לקמן מנחות פח.): "למנחה — ולוג שמן":
Rashi on Menachot 9b:10:1.english: Fine flour of an tenth [of an ephah] - It requires a log of oil, as it says in the chapter [entitled] Shtei Middot (below, Menachot 88a): "For the meal offering — and a log of oil."

Rashi on Menachot 9b:11:1.hebrew: (מן המנחה) והנותרת מן המנחה פרט לשחסרה היא - דמנחה שלימה משמע:
Rashi on Menachot 9b:11:1.english: (from the meal offering) “But that which is left of the meal offering” — excluding one that was itself lacking - For [the word “meal offering”] implies a complete meal offering.

Rashi on Menachot 9b:11:2.hebrew: ושחסר קומצה - דשירי מנחה העשויה כהלכתה משמע. וקומץ החסר, נפקא לן בהקומץ רבה (לקמן מנחות דף כז.) דפסול, מדכתיב "מלא קומצו" תרי זימני:
Rashi on Menachot 9b:11:2.english: Or whose handful was lacking - For "the remainder of the meal offering" implies a meal offering that was prepared properly. And [the case of] a deficient handful, we derive from [the chapter] Hakometz Rabba (below, Menachot 27a) that it is disqualified, since it is written "its full handful" twice.

Rashi on Menachot 9b:11:3.hebrew: ושלא הקטיר מלבונתה כלום - נפקא בהקומץ רבה (לקמן מנחות דף כז.) דהקטרת לבונה וקומץ (מעכבות זו את זו):
Rashi on Menachot 9b:11:3.english: Or from which [the priest] did not burn any of its frankincense - This is derived in [the chapter] Hakometz Rabbah (later, Menachot 27a), [from the principle] that the burning of the frankincense and the handful (are each indispensable to the other):

Rashi on Menachot 9b:11:4.hebrew: מלבונתה כלום - אבל אם הקטיר קצת, נאכלים השירים, כדאמר לקמן בהאי פירקא (מנחות דף יב.) דאם חסרה בשעת הקטרה, כשרה:
Rashi on Menachot 9b:11:4.english: Any of its frankincense - But if he burned some [of it], the remainders are eaten, as it says later in this chapter (Menachot 12a) that if [the meal offering] became lacking at the time of the burning, it is valid.

Rashi on Menachot 9b:12:1.hebrew: תרי קראי - מסולת ומן המנחה. אבל משמנה לא חשיב, דהאי לגופיה אתא, לקודם קמיצה. אבל בסולת, למה לי תרי קראי:
Rashi on Menachot 9b:12:1.english: Two verses - [One from] "of the fine flour" and [one from] "of the meal offering." But [the verse] "of its oil" he does not count, for that one comes for its own purpose, [namely] for [a deficiency] before the removal of the handful. But with regard to the fine flour, why do I need two verses?

Rashi on Menachot 9b:12:2.hebrew: לאו לקודם קמיצה - דלא יביא מתוך ביתו וימלאנה:
Rashi on Menachot 9b:12:2.english: Is it not [that one verse refers] to [a meal offering that became lacking] before the removal of the handful - That one may not bring [flour] from his house and fill it up.

Rashi on Menachot 9b:12:3.hebrew: לשירים שחסרו - לומר דאין מקטירין קומץ עליהם:
Rashi on Menachot 9b:12:3.english: For the remainders that became lacking - [This teaches] that one may not burn the handful on account of them.

Rashi on Menachot 9b:14:1.hebrew: אסורים באכילה - דהאי קרא דמן המנחה לא משתעי אלא בשירים:
Rashi on Menachot 9b:14:1.english: Prohibited for consumption - For this verse, [the phrase] "from the meal offering," speaks only of the remainder.

Rashi on Menachot 9b:16:1.hebrew: נותרת מן הנותרת - (כגון) דמתחילה היו כל השירים נותרות מן הקומץ, וכשחסרו שירים, היו הנותרים שירי שירים:
Rashi on Menachot 9b:16:1.english: The remainder of the remainder - [This applies] where, initially, all the leftovers were remainders from the handful, and when some of the leftovers became lacking, the remaining [portions] were the leftovers of the leftovers.

Rashi on Menachot 9b:16:2.hebrew: שהיתה כבר - בשעת הקומץ היתה שלימה, אע"פ שחסרה בין קמיצה להקטרה, קרינא ביה "והנותרת מן המנחה". ופליג ר' ינאי אדזעירי. ל"א: שהיתה כבר בשעת הקטרה, והכי משמע: "והנותרת מן המנחה" שהיתה שלימה כבר בשעה שנעשו אלו שירים — יאכלו אהרן ובניו; אבל לא יאכלו אותם שירים שנעשו שירים ממנחה חסירה. והיינו דזעירי, ומשמעות דורשין איכא בינייהו (בן בתירא אומר קומץ לתוך הכלי ויחזור ויקמוץ בימין):
Rashi on Menachot 9b:16:2.english: That was previously - At the time of the handful, it was whole; even though it became deficient between the taking of the handful and the burning, we read of it, "But that which is left of the meal offering." And Rabbi Yannai disagrees with Ze'eiri. Another explanation: "that was previously" [whole] at the time of the burning, and this is what it means: "But that which is left of the meal offering" that was already whole at the time when these became remainders — Aaron and his sons shall eat; but they may not eat those remainders that became remainders from a deficient meal offering. And this is [the same as] Ze'eiri's [view], and [the difference between them is] the manner of interpretive derivation [i.e., which words of the verse are expounded]. (Ben Beterah says: He should take the handful into the vessel, and take the handful again with the right hand.)

Rashi on Menachot 9b:18:1.english: For itself - [It is needed to teach that the oil is poured on] the left [hand] and not the right.

Rashi on Menachot 9b:18:2.hebrew: שמאלית אחרינא כתיב - נמי, בפרשת מצורע לעשיר:
Rashi on Menachot 9b:18:2.english: Another 'left' is written - also [in the passage dealing] with the wealthy [leper].

Rashi on Menachot 9b:19:1.hebrew: ואימא - להכי אתא שמאל אחרינא, למיעוט אחר מיעוט, דמתרוייהו שמעינן ימנית לא. והא דקאמרת ואין מיעוט אחר מיעוט אלא לרבות, הוא דאפי' ימין דכהן כשרה בשמן דמצורע:
Rashi on Menachot 9b:19:1.english: But say - [Perhaps] this is why another [mention of] "left" came: for a restriction after a restriction, [so that] from both of them we learn [that] the right [hand] is not [valid]. [But] "a restriction after a restriction serves only to amplify" [means] that even the right hand of the priest is valid for the oil of the leper.

Rashi on Menachot 9b:19:2.hebrew: שמאלית אחרינא כתיב - בעני. ואי משמע מיעוט אחר מיעוט, תלתא למה לי:
Rashi on Menachot 9b:19:2.english: Another "left" is written - regarding the poor [leper]. And if [the verse] implied [that] one restriction after another [restriction serves to amplify], why do I need three [mentions of the left hand]?

Rashi on Menachot 9b:1:1.english: A meal offering — what is it doing [here]? - What sprinkling is there in a meal offering?

Rashi on Menachot 9b:1:2.hebrew: במנחת נסכים - הבאים עם הזבח. אם אבד חלב ובשר של זבח, ומנחה קיימת, לא יזרוק הדם של הזבח מן המנחה:
Rashi on Menachot 9b:1:2.english: With the meal offering of libations - [the libations] that come with the slaughtered offering. If the fat and the flesh of the slaughtered offering were lost, but the meal offering remains, he should not sprinkle the blood [of the slaughtered offering] on account of the meal offering.

Rashi on Menachot 9b:20:1.hebrew: ארבע שמאלית כתיבי - חד לגופיה, וחד לגלויי עלייהו דהנך תרתי דלאו למיעוט אחר מיעוט אתו, וחד שלא תאמר האי דקמיה להכי אתא, מה כאן שמאלית אף בעלמא שמאלית, דא"כ האי בתרא למה לי: אלא מדכתיב האי בתרא הוי להו שני כתובים הבאין כאחד, ואין מלמדין. לשון אחר: שמאלית תרי לגופייהו, חד בעני וחד לעשיר, שלא תאמר הואיל ואשתני בעניות אישתני בימין, ותרי לאשמועי' כאן שמאלית ולא אחר, דהוו להו שני כתובין, דאי כתיב חד הוה אמינא מה כאן שמאלית אף בעלמא יד שמאלית. ואין מיעוט אחר מיעוט נמי ליכא לאקשויי, דהא מכולהו שמעינן מינה ימנית לא, וא"כ כל הני למה לי. הני לישני לא נהירא, דכל שני כתובין הבאין כאחד שבהש"ס אין דומין לאלו. דכי אמרינן אין מלמדין, הני מילי כשגילה שני כתובין בשני דברים, דאמרי' דאי ניחא למילף מינייהו נכתוב חד ונילף אידך מיניה. אבל הכא דבחדא מילתא כתיבי, אינן שני דברים הבאין כאחד, אלא קראי יתירי נינהו. ונראה בעיני דמדכתיב כל הנך יתירא ילפינן לה: כאן גילה לך שמאלית, אבל בעלמא כל כף הוה ימין. דאי למילף מה כאן שמאלית אף בעלמא שמאלית, מכדי דאם אינו ענין כאן תנהו ענין לכל המקומות הוא, ואם כן בחדא יתירא סגי. ונכתוב תלתא ונשתוק: חד לגופיה, וחד מה כאן שמאלית וכו', וחד שלא תאמר מיעוט אחר מיעוט הוא:
Rashi on Menachot 9b:20:1.english: Four [mentions of] "left" are written - One for its own sake; and one to reveal about those other two that they do not come as a limitation following a limitation; and one so that you should not say that the one before it came for this purpose — "just as here [it is] the left, so too elsewhere [it is] the left" — for if so, why do I need this last one? Rather, since this last one is written, they become two verses that come as one, and we do not derive from [such verses]. Another explanation: "Left" [appears] twice for their own sake, one for a poor person and one for a rich person, so that you should not say, "Since he has changed in poverty, he has changed with regard to the right [hand]"; and two to teach, "Here [it is] the left, and not another," for they are two verses [that come as one], since if only one were written I would have said, "Just as here [it is] the left hand, so too elsewhere [it is] the left hand." And [as for] "a limitation following a limitation," there is also no need to raise a difficulty, for from all of them we learn that the right [hand] is not [used]; and if so, why do I need all of these? These explanations are not clear, for all "two verses that come as one" found in the Talmud are not like these. For when we say "we do not derive," this applies only when [Scripture] revealed two verses in two matters, as we say that if it were agreeable to derive from them, let it write one and let us derive the other from it. But here, where they are written about a single matter, they are not two matters coming as one, but rather superfluous verses. And it appears to me that from the fact that all these superfluous [mentions] are written, we derive: here [Scripture] revealed to you [that it is] the left, but elsewhere every palm is [presumed to be] the right. For if [it were] to derive "just as here [it is] the left, so too elsewhere [it is] the left," since [the principle is that] if it is not relevant here, apply it to all places — and if so, one superfluous [mention] would suffice. Let it write three and be silent: one for its own sake, and one [for] "just as here [it is] the left," etc., and one so that you should not say, "It is a limitation following a limitation."

Rashi on Menachot 9b:21:1.hebrew: אמר ליה ר' ירמיה - לר' זירא: כיון דדרשת (כל השנוי בפרשת מצורע עני לדרשה), כל שמאלית דמצורע דריש נמי. ואם כן, "על בהן ידו הימנית ועל בהן רגלו הימנית" למה לי — בין בשמן מצורע עשיר, בין בעני:
Rashi on Menachot 9b:21:1.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said to him - to Rabbi Zeira: Since you interpret homiletically (everything repeated in the passage of the leper — of the poor leper — for a homiletical teaching), interpret every [mention of the] left [hand] of the leper as well. [If so,] why do I need "upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the big toe of his right foot" — whether with the oil of a wealthy leper or of a poor one?

Rashi on Menachot 9b:21:2.hebrew: למה לי - כיון דכתיב "על דם האשם יתן את השמן", אנא ידענא דעל ידו הימנית היא, דהא כתב בענין בהן יד ורגל בדם האשם לעיל מיניה:
Rashi on Menachot 9b:21:2.english: Why do I [need it]? - Since it is written, “upon the blood of the guilt-offering he shall place the oil,” I know that it is [placed] on his right hand, for it already wrote the thumb of the hand and the big toe of the foot with respect to the blood of the guilt-offering, earlier than it.

Rashi on Menachot 9b:3:1.hebrew: והרים הכהן מן המנחה את אזכרתה והקטיר המזבחה - עד דאיתא לכולה המנחה קיימת. ואי לא, לא יקטיר (את אזכרתה):
Rashi on Menachot 9b:3:1.english: "And the priest shall remove from the meal offering its memorial part, and shall make it smoke upon the altar" - Until all of it [the meal offering] is intact; and if not, he shall not burn [its memorial part].

Rashi on Menachot 9b:4:1.hebrew: שהיתה כבר - שהיתה כבר שלימה בשעת הקומץ, אע"ג דהשתא אינה שלימה, יקטיר:
Rashi on Menachot 9b:4:1.english: That was already - That was already whole at the time of the removal of the handful, [then] even though now it is not whole, he shall burn [the handful].

Rashi on Menachot 9b:5:1.hebrew: ומקטיר בזיכין - אלמא, שירים שחסרו בין (סילוק) קמיצה להקטרה — מקטירים עלייהו הקומץ:
Rashi on Menachot 9b:5:1.english: And he burns the bowls [of frankincense] - Evidently, with remainders [of a meal offering] that became deficient between the removal of the handful and its burning, one [still] burns the handful on account of them.

Rashi on Menachot 9b:5:2.hebrew: ואמר ר"א כו' - לא איצטריך למתנייה אלא איידי דתנא לעיל, תנא הכא:
Rashi on Menachot 9b:5:2.english: And Rabbi Elazar said, etc. - [This statement] was not needed [to be taught] except that, since [the Tanna] taught [it] above, he taught [it] here as well.

Rashi on Menachot 9b:6:1.english: A complete Mishnah - An unattributed Mishnah [i.e., a teaching stated anonymously].

Rashi on Menachot 9b:8:1.hebrew: מישתרי טומאה לגבייהו - דכתיב בתמיד (במדבר כח) במועדו, ומשמע אפילו בשבת וטומאה:
Rashi on Menachot 9b:8:1.english: Ritual impurity was permitted for them - For it is written regarding the daily offering (Numbers 28), "in its appointed time," and this implies even on Shabbat and in a state of ritual impurity.

Rashi on Menachot 9b:8:2.hebrew: זאת אומרת - מדלא שני הכי, שמע מינה חסרון כבעל מום דמי, ואין בעל מום שרי בצבור טפי מביחיד. הלכך, חסרון דבין קמיצה להקטרה, אי הוי פסול ביחיד, הוה פסול נמי בצבור. הלכך אישתיק:
Rashi on Menachot 9b:8:2.english: This implies - Since [Reish Lakish] did not answer this way, learn from it that a deficiency is considered like a blemish, and a blemished [animal] is not permitted for a communal [offering] any more than for an individual [offering]. Therefore, [regarding] a deficiency between the removal of the handful and the burning [of it], if it is disqualifying for an individual, it is also disqualifying for the community. Therefore, he was silent.

Rashi on Menachot 9b:9:1.hebrew: להא שמעתא - דאישתיק ריש לקיש ולא שני ליה לרבי יוחנן "צבור שאני":
Rashi on Menachot 9b:9:1.english: Concerning this halakha - That [Reish Lakish] was silent and did not answer [Rabbi Yoḥanan] by saying, "A communal [offering] is different."

Rashi on Menachot 9b:9:2.hebrew: מי לא עסקינן - (דמשום) פלוגתא דלעיל, דכי נמי קאמר ר"ל אין מקטירין קומץ עליהם — במנחת צבור נמי אמר, כגון בזיכים דלחם הפנים:
Rashi on Menachot 9b:9:2.english: Are we not dealing - (because of) the disagreement above, [namely,] that even when Reish Lakish says that one does not burn the handful on account of them [i.e., a deficient meal offering], he said it also regarding a communal meal offering, such as the bowls [of frankincense] of the showbread:

Tosafot on Menachot 9b:14:1.hebrew: אותן שיריים אסורין באכילה - וא"ת כיון דאסירי, הרי הוא כאילו לא נשתייר כלום, והיאך מקטיר קומץ עליהם? הא בכל זבחים קא"ר יהושע דהיכא דלא נשתייר כלום דאין זורק הדם. וי"ל כיון דילפינן מנחה מזבח תהא כזבח, דכיון דלא אבדו הוי כאילו הן בעין. וצריך לחלק בין זה לנטמא, דכיון דאין זבח נפסל ע"י חסרון, אע"ג דשיריים נפסלין, עבדינן ליה כזבח להקטיר קומץ עליהם:
Tosafot on Menachot 9b:14:1.english: "That remainder is prohibited for consumption" - If you say: Since [the remainder] is prohibited, it is as if nothing remained at all, so how can one burn the handful on account of it? Surely Rabbi Yehoshua said in [the chapter] Kol HaZevachim that where nothing remained, one does not throw the blood. And one can say: Since we derive [the law of] a meal offering from an animal offering, it should be like an animal offering, for since [the remainder] was not lost, it is as if it were present. And one must distinguish between this [case] and [the case of a remainder that] became impure: for since an animal offering is not disqualified through lacking, even though the remainder [of a meal offering] is disqualified, we treat it like an animal offering, to burn the handful on account of it:

Tosafot on Menachot 9b:15:1.hebrew: אותן שיריים מה הן באכילה - הוה מצי למיפשטה מהא דאם משנפרקה נפרס לחמה, הלחם פסול:
Tosafot on Menachot 9b:15:1.english: What is the status of those remainders with regard to eating - [The Gemara] could have resolved [this dilemma] from [the ruling] that if [the bread's] loaf was broken [into pieces] after it was taken apart, [the offering's] bread is disqualified:

Tosafot on Menachot 9b:19:1.hebrew: אין מיעוט אחר מיעוט אלא לרבות - ואם תאמר: ולשתוק מתרוייהו? וכי האי גוונא מצי להקשות בכל מיעוט אחר מיעוט:
Tosafot on Menachot 9b:19:1.english: "One restriction after another restriction serves only to amplify" - And if you say: Let [the Torah] be silent about both [of the mentions of "left"]? [If so,] in this manner one could ask [a question] about every case of one restriction after another restriction.

Tosafot on Menachot 9b:21:1.hebrew: על בהן ידו הימנית כו' - בין דעני בין דעשיר קא בעי. דכיון דכתיב "על דם האשם" ו"על מקום דם האשם", ממילא ידעינן בשמן. וה"ה דמצי למיבעי "מתנוך אוזן". ולפי שהתחיל לדרוש "כף" דמצורע, קא מסיק ושאל "על בהן" מאי דרשת ביה, בין דעני בין דעשיר:
Tosafot on Menachot 9b:21:1.english: "Upon the thumb of his right hand," etc. - He is asking [about the verse] both for the poor leper and for the wealthy one. For since it is written "upon the blood of the guilt offering" and "upon the place of the blood of the guilt offering," we know about the oil automatically. And by the same reasoning, he could have asked about "the tip of the ear." But because he began to expound the word "palm" [written] regarding the leper, he concludes [by asking] about "upon the thumb": what do you derive from it, both for the poor leper and for the wealthy one?
